setup.title: Setup
setup.configured: The assistant is configured — /webhook is active.
setup.welcome_intro: This is the iTop AI Assistant setup wizard. The next steps connect the assistant to your iTop and LLM, and get the system ready to run.
setup.security_copy_alert: Copy the tokens now — they are shown only this once. The admin token is saved to this browser automatically; the webhook token is written into the iTop webhook configuration at the iTop webhooks step (X-Auth-Token header).
setup.security_admin_token_desc: Bearer token for this UI and the /api endpoints
setup.itop_account_note: The account needs the REST Services User profile and is used as the AI service account — its comments must be distinguishable from engineers.
setup.webhooks_desc: Creates the triggers and webhooks in iTop that call this assistant on ticket creation and public log updates. Requires an iTop administrator account — the credentials are used for this one operation and are not stored anywhere. Existing objects are left untouched. This step is optional: the same objects can be created manually (see README) or with the CLI.
setup.llm_base_url_desc: Endpoint address; the placeholder shows the usual one for this provider
setup.llm_provider_desc: How the model is reached — pick the API, not the model
setup.llm_model_desc: Model name as exposed by the endpoint
setup.llm_api_key_desc: Required by cloud providers; local servers ignore it
setup.final_complete_detail: If you ran the iTop webhooks step, iTop is already calling {{origin}}/webhook. If you skipped it, configure the triggers and webhooks manually (see README) or from the Connections screen — the webhook token goes in the X-Auth-Token header and the trigger context must exclude REST/JSON.

connections.title: Connections
connections.mapping_desc: How each object family's semantics map onto your iTop datamodel — edit this instead of the code when iTop has been customized. An attribute that is mapped but does not exist in your iTop is not ignored: the read asks for it and the whole sweep of that family fails, so mark what your datamodel lacks as absent.
connections.reset_confirm: Reset the "{{section}}" section to env/yaml defaults?
connections.webhooks_desc: Creates the triggers and webhooks in iTop that call this assistant (uses the saved webhook token). Requires an iTop administrator account — the credentials are used once and never stored. Existing objects are left untouched.
connections.security_desc: Tokens are write-only: the current values are never shown. Use the generate buttons to create a strong random token, then copy it before saving.
connections.security_webhook_token_desc: Set the same value in the iTop Remote Application Connection (X-Auth-Token header)
connections.security_admin_token_desc: Bearer token for this UI and the /api endpoints; saved to this browser automatically
connections.clear_admin_token_confirm: Clear the admin token? The admin API becomes open to anyone who can reach it.
connections.clear_webhook_token_confirm: Clear the webhook token? /webhook will accept unauthenticated requests.
connections.llm_base_url_desc: Endpoint address; the placeholder shows the usual one for this provider
connections.llm_model_desc: Model name as exposed by the endpoint
connections.llm_api_key_desc: Required by cloud providers; local servers ignore it
connections.llm_think_tags_desc: Tag names stripped as inline reasoning blocks
connections.llm_provider_desc: How the model is reached — pick the API, not the model
connections.llm_params_desc: JSON passed to the client as-is: temperature, max_tokens, timeout, …
connections.llm_tool_choice_desc: vLLM, LiteLLM and LM Studio accept it; DeepSeek returns an error. Verify with Test LLM.
connections.llm_tool_choice_rejected: The endpoint rejected the forced tool_choice — turn the switch off: {{error}}
connections.llm_no_tool_calling: The endpoint answers, but the model did not call the tool. The assistant needs a model that calls tools reliably. {{error}}
connections.embeddings_base_url_desc: The full OpenAI-compatible prefix your provider documents for embeddings, not a bare host:port. For Ollama: http://localhost:11434/v1 — not the bare host:port used for the LLM chat connection. For Google's Gemini API: https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai.
connections.embeddings_model_desc: Embedding model as exposed by the endpoint; must be multilingual, e.g. bge-m3
connections.embeddings_dimension_mismatch: The endpoint returned dimension {{actual}} but the config says {{expected}} — fix the Dimension field
connections.embeddings_rebuild_warning: Vectors of two models cannot be compared, so the sweep fills a replacement collection from scratch for every indexed family ({{families}}) — every indexed object has its vectors computed again, at whatever your endpoint charges for it. Until a family's replacement is complete, searches over it are refused, so whatever relies on them is left without similar tickets and knowledge base articles. Putting the previous model and dimension back before the rebuild finishes discards the half-filled replacement — the live index is never touched while one is being built.
connections.embeddings_rebuild_confirm: Changing the embeddings model or dimension computes the vectors of everything indexed again ({{families}}) and refuses searches over those families until the rebuild finishes. Save anyway?
connections.class_overrides_desc: Point differences between the ticket classes, merged over the fields above: {"Incident": {"request_type": null}}. Only the semantic names listed above are accepted.

modules.title: Modules
modules.saved: Saved — applies from the next processed ticket
modules.reset_confirm: Reset the "{{name}}" config to env/yaml defaults?
modules.check_fields: Some values were rejected — see the fields below
modules.dry_run_title: Dry run — nothing is written to iTop
modules.dry_run_desc: Modules keep running as they would in production — tickets are classified, questions and handoff notes are composed, the run journal records every step — but no field change and no log entry reaches iTop. Applies from the next run; the state of a ticket is kept as in production, so a ticket processed dry is not picked up again once the mode is off.

vector.title: Vector index
vector.fingerprint_mismatch: The index was built with a different embeddings model or dimension, and the family it belongs to is not being indexed — switch it back on for the rebuild to start, or put the previous model back.
vector.rebuild_running: The embeddings model changed, so the index is being rebuilt. A new version is being filled next to the live one and takes over when it is complete — nothing to do but wait. Searches over that family are refused meanwhile, since vectors from two models cannot be compared.
vector.rebuild_pending: The embeddings model changed. The next sweep pass starts filling a replacement version next to the live one — nothing to do but wait. Searches over that family are refused meanwhile, since vectors from two models cannot be compared.
vector.rebuild_hint: Version being filled for the new embeddings model. It replaces the active one once a sweep pass has finished it.
vector.family_not_configured_hint: This family is no longer configured — its collection is unused and a candidate for cleanup.
vector.family_disabled_hint: Indexing is switched off for this family on the Indexed classes tab. Its collection is kept but no longer updated.
vector.index_none: No active index yet — it is created on the first sweep.
vector.sweep_hint: Runs the next incremental pass immediately instead of waiting for the sweep interval — only objects changed since the last pass are re-embedded.
vector.reindex_confirm: Rebuild the entire index? Every object will be re-embedded — this can take a while and load the embeddings endpoint.
vector.field_index_values_desc: Values of the class's relevance attribute (e.g. status) that keep an object in the index; empty = index every object
vector.field_acl_org_fields_desc: Semantic fields whose values say which organizations may see an object of this class. A search narrows its candidates to objects sharing an organization with whoever is asking; an object naming none is left to the rights check under that person's own token, which decides either way.
vector.acl_changed_title: This reaches the index only on a full pass
vector.acl_changed_warning: Objects already indexed keep the organizations they were indexed with until the sweep visits them again — and changing a link set in iTop does not necessarily move the object's modification date, so the incremental sweep may never notice. Run a full reindex after saving. It costs no embeddings: the text has not changed, only the payload is rewritten.
vector.acl_changed_confirm: Access settings changed. Already-indexed objects keep the old ones until a full pass rewrites them. Save anyway?
vector.acl_backfill_offer: Saved. Rebuild the whole index now so the new access settings reach objects already indexed? Nothing is re-embedded — only the payload is rewritten.
vector.fragments_explainer: An object is indexed as several fragments, matched separately: a query can look like another ticket's description without looking like its solution. Which fragments exist, and what they may contain, is defined by the source — you choose which fields go into each.
vector.families_explainer: Classes are grouped by family — one family is one Qdrant collection. Add a class to whichever family should index it.
vector.family_source_unknown: No registered source matches this family name — it was likely removed from the code. Its saved classes are kept but cannot be configured here; remove the family if it was added by mistake.
vector.field_family_enabled_desc: Off: the sweep skips it and searches over it are refused. The collection is kept, so switching it back on resumes where it stopped.
vector.field_family_override_desc: Blank = use the system-wide value from the Indexer tab
vector.fragment_source_defined: Content is defined by the source
vector.fragment_off: No fields — this fragment is not indexed
vector.visibility_internal_hint: Engineer-only content. Searches run on behalf of a caller never return it.
vector.unknown_fragment: "{{kind}}" is not a fragment this source produces — it is indexed as nothing. Remove it to save.
vector.unknown_fields: Fields this source does not provide: {{fields}}. Remove them to save.
vector.nothing_indexed: No fragment is enabled for this class: it will be swept and produce no chunks at all.
vector.field_enabled_desc: Applies from the next sweep, no restart needed
vector.field_max_chunks_per_object_hint: An object chunking past this is skipped without being embedded and counted separately — it is junk (an inlined attachment), not a long article.

system.title: System
system.telemetry_desc: One aggregate document is sent per day, containing information about how the system is used: counters, enabled modules, and the versions it runs on. No information about ticket content, names, addresses, or keys is ever transmitted.
system.telemetry_appeal: This is the only way to find out how actively the assistant is being used, which of its features deserve further development, and which issues need attention first. Since this is an open-source project with no sales team to ask these questions, this remains the only channel available. Please leave this feature enabled unless you have a good reason to disable it.
system.not_a_release_build: This build was not published by us, so no data is transmitted. Telemetry is sent only from officially published builds.
